meta.title: Deep-Layer Attention Pruning for Vision-Language Models

units.text: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress on multimodal understanding tasks by processing images as sequences of visual tokens within large language model decoders [cite].
units.found_note: two or more works cited together

units.text: Visual token pruning—selectively retaining only the most relevant tokens—has emerged as a promising solution for efficient VLM inference [cite].
units.found_note: two or more works cited together

units.text: Existing pruning methods face a fundamental challenge: attention-based importance scoring, while computationally convenient, can fail catastrophically on spatially-sensitive tasks like visual grounding [cite].
units.found_note: two or more works cited together

units.text: FastV [cite], which prunes tokens based on shallow-layer attention, achieves only 33.85% grounding accuracy on RefCOCO benchmarks—less than half of the unpruned model's performance.
units.s2: cited here: FastV · no other work cited or named

units.text: D²Pruner [cite] addresses this by debiasing attention scores using an offline prior computed from 1000 COCO images, improving accuracy to 55.03%.

units.text: FastV [cite] pioneered training-free pruning by selecting tokens based on attention scores from shallow layers, but suffers from significant performance degradation on spatially-sensitive tasks.
units.s2: cited here: FastV · no other work cited or named

units.text: LLaVA-PruMerge [cite] combines pruning with token merging to preserve information from discarded tokens, while PyramidDrop [cite] progressively reduces tokens across layers following a pyramid schedule.
units.found_note: two or more works cited together

units.text: SparseVLM [cite] introduces text-aware sparsification that conditions token selection on the input query, and FEATHER [cite] revisits pruning strategies with improved layer selection.
units.found_note: two or more works cited together

units.text: Token Merging (ToMe) [cite], originally designed for Vision Transformers, has also been adapted for VLM acceleration.

units.text: Recent work has explored more sophisticated selection criteria: Balanced Token Pruning [cite] optimizes global token allocation across layers, while IVC-Prune [cite] leverages implicit visual coordinates for pruning decisions.

units.text: D²Pruner [cite] advances this approach by introducing debiased importance scoring with Maximal Independent Set (MIS) for diversity-aware token selection.

units.text: PoRe [cite] addresses position bias through reweighting schemes, while recent analysis [cite] reveals that visual information flow in MLLMs varies significantly across layers, suggesting that layer choice is critical for attention-based pruning.
